posture: Inform — a clean Monday scan that picks up the weekend: no fresh, dated NSW-REZ development cleared the relevance bar in the roughly 60 hours from Friday evening to Monday morning. EnergyCo's latest-updates feed, the AEMO market-notices feed, the New England network-operator and corridor pages, and the Central-West Orana and ACEREZ pages all held no new dated material in the window, and no developer disclosure, planning step or regional-masthead item carried a fresh REZ nexus. One thread that surfaced prominently in the scan resolves to stale material and is dropped: RenewEconomy's account of the NSW cumulative-impact studies for the Central-West Orana, South West and New England REZs (five reports each on workforce accommodation, water and wastewater, skills, supply chain and waste, with two due for public release 'in the coming months') is dated 19 September 2025 and is well outside the window — a standing federal/state-process thread rather than breaking news, though the promised public release of the CWO and New England studies is worth tracking. Everything heavier is an unchanged prior-digest carry-forward and is deduplicated out: the NSW Farmers Association's formally carried energy-transition motions (cut the New England REZ from 8GW to 3GW, oppose compulsory acquisition of land for transmission, oblige EnergyCo to reassess all REZ transmission requirements, plus anti-subsidy and baseline soil/water-testing motions) and Rebecca Reardon's presidency; Minister Sharpe's $14.5m Central-West Orana Telecommunications Infrastructure Uplift Program; Squadron Energy's 16 July Boorolong exit and the New England political fight; the New England Draft REZ Access Scheme Declaration on exhibition (feedback by 6 August, declaration targeted end-September, EIS expected in the second half of 2026, energisation targeted 2032); the refined 1km Muswellbrook-Walcha corridor and its July-September field-investigation program across roughly 150 affected landholders amid Walcha High Country Guardians opposition and the 22,000-signature petition; EnergyCo's 15 July South West REZ Project Development Deed with Transgrid (Jerilderie-Wagga Wagga, unlocking 3.56GW); the South West REZ $60m Community and Employment Benefit Program consultation (online survey, 3 August webinar, drop-in sessions at Jerilderie and Coleambally on 12 August and Darlington Point on 20 August); the Illawarra REZ Community Reference Group call; and on Central-West Orana the Port-to-REZ OSOM delivery campaign with turbine-blade deliveries to Uungula underway this month, the Main Road No. 709 gazettal, and ACEREZ's staged access-track works under stronger heritage controls with the DPHI rock-shelter assessment still open, plus the community roadshow flagged for 11-15 August. Source gaps to log rather than read as absence of news: ABC News, The Guardian Australia and the paid mastheads (AFR, SMH, the ACM regional titles) surfaced no new dated REZ headline in this run even at standfirst level, so no paywalled items are carried today. Nothing in the scan changes the standing posture: the dominant exposures remain the New England political and social-licence contest ahead of the March 2027 state election, and the delivery and heritage risks on Central-West Orana.
summary: A clean Monday scan across the weekend window: no fresh NSW-REZ item cleared the relevance bar from Friday evening to Monday 27 July morning, with no new EnergyCo release, AEMO market notice, planning step or developer disclosure carrying a REZ nexus. The most prominent thread to surface resolves to stale material and is dropped: RenewEconomy's piece on the NSW cumulative-impact studies for the three inland REZs is dated 19 September 2025, a standing process thread rather than breaking news (the promised public release of the CWO and New England studies remains worth tracking). All other active threads — the NSW Farmers carried motions and Reardon presidency, Sharpe's $14.5m Central-West Orana telco uplift, the Squadron Boorolong exit, the New England Access Scheme exhibition (feedback by 6 August), the July-September corridor field investigations and Walcha opposition, the 15 July South West Transgrid deed, the South West $60m community-benefit consultation, the Illawarra Community Reference Group call, and the Central-West Orana OSOM delivery, Main Road No. 709 gazettal and ACEREZ heritage matter — are prior-digest carry-forwards and are deduplicated out. ABC News, The Guardian Australia and the paid mastheads (AFR, SMH, ACM titles) surfaced no new dated REZ item and are logged as a source gap. The digest is published with empty sections so the archive shows continuity — itself a useful 'ran clean' signal.
